utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Good afternoon everyone. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This case number IT-08-91-PT the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can I check first of all, Mr. Zupljanin, can you hear me, are you receiving interpretation in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] I hear you loud and clear, Your Honour, and yes I am receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Please let me know if at any point in time you are not. I understand Mr. Stanisic is appearing via videolink from Belgrade. Can you hear me in Belgrade? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And you're receiving interpretation -- Mr. Stanisic is receiving interpretation in language he understands? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, my name is Tom Hannis and Karen Beausey and our case manager, Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you all. For Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thomas Visnjic attorney at law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honour, Pantelic co-counsel for Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. And in Belgrade, with Mr. Stanisic? We have a picture now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Slobodan Cvijetic -- yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you all of you as well. The purpose of today's hearing is twofold, really. This is the first status conference in the present case as a result of the decision of the Trial Chamber ordering joinder of the cases against Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Zupljanin, and as a result we have had prior status conferences, 11, for Mr. Stanisic in the previous indictment and one initial appearance and one further appearance from Mr. Zupljanin in the previous indictment as well. So this is the first status conference, as I say, on that joint indictment, and obviously for the normal purposes of a status conference, any exchanges on issues for trial preparation as well as checking on issues related to the accused condition of detention and conditions generally. But as well, this afternoon and this is the first matter I'd like to deal with, in light of the decision of the Trial Chamber on the 23rd of September, we allowed for the joinder and as well amendments to the indictment, and resulting from those amendments were new charges and therefore we need to have in essence a further appearance this afternoon for the purpose of taking pleas in relation to the operative indictment. And that was filed on the 29th of September 2008. Those pleas will relate only to the new charges which have been permitted by the Trial Chamber's ruling. So if I could proceed to that immediately. Perhaps we'll deal first of all with Mr. Stanisic in Belgrade. Both accused of course have the right to have the new charges read out to them, if they wish. So I'll begin, Mr. Stanisic or counsel, does he wish to have the new charges read out or is he prepared to waive the reading? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] No need to read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my client is familiar with the indictment and there is no need to have them read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will proceed then first of all with the pleas on those new charges in relation to you, Mr. Stanisic. For your alleged responsibility under Articles 7 (1) and 7 (3), two crime sites have been added under count on persecution, the unlawful detention in the Batkovic camp in the municipality of Bijeljina and an alleged mass killing on a bridge in Kotlina in the municipality of Gacko. Mr. Stanisic, how do you plead to count 1 as it now stands? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Further, the said alleged mass killing on a bridge in Kotlina in the municipality of Gacko has also been added under -- yes, I'm sorry, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise Your Honour, my client cannot hear so could we fix it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Thank you for bringing that to my attention. You are not receiving sound or you are not receiving interpretation? One moment, Mr. Stanisic, we appear to have a problem here in The Hague. THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving Mr. Stanisic's sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: We'll try this once again. We've recorded a plea in relation to count 1 already, Mr. Stanisic. How do you plead to count 2 as to now stands? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. Now Mr. Zupljanin is indicating that he is receiving sound and translation. But now the Prosecution may have some difficulty. No, they are fine. Okay. So everyone apparently is receiving. And thank you again for bringing that to my attention. Mr. Stanisic, similarly, relation to count 3 and count 4 as they both now stand, it is the same alleged mass killing which has been added as a crime site. To those two counts, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Registrar, you may note the not guilty pleas entered to counts 1 through 4 on behalf of Mr. Stanisic. Mr. Zupljanin, and since you are here, if you could please stand for the pleas in your case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: First I should verify, does he wish to have the charges read to him, the indictment read, or is he prepared to waive the reading of the indictment, counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I take it that means no to my first questions which was --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The first question, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin, for your alleged responsibility under Articles 7 (1) and 7 (3) two crime sites have been added under count 1 on persecution, the unlawful detention at the Ljubija football stadium in the municipality of Prijedor and at the prison in Sanski Most in the municipality of Sanski Most. Mr. Zupljanin, how do you plead to count 1 as it now stands? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Mrs. Prost. Not guilty on this count of the indictment or any other for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to the alleged mistreatment of detainees at the football stadium and at the prison in Sanski Most, they have also been added under counts 5 to 8 relating to torture, cruel treatment, and inhumane acts. I will deal with these as a group, Mr. Zupljanin, given your comment, so in relation to counts 5, 6, 7 and 8 as they now stand, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty. Not under any of the counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Registrar, could you please note the not guilty pleas on counts 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8 for Mr. Zupljanin. All right. We'll proceed then to the second item that I have noted, Mr. Hannis if I could turn to you at this stage in relation just to one pending motion. On the 17th of November counsel for Mr. Zupljanin filed a motion challenging the form of the indictment. A similar motion has already been filed by Mr. Stanisic and replied to. The Trial Chamber is inquiring whether the Prosecution might be in a position to file the response perhaps within a shorter time limit than is normally the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would request to have the full time. This Defence motion asks for extended word limits, there's 3800 words, it's substantial, we feel like we need the full amount of time to reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis, that's understandable and it is of course an important motion, so we felt it appropriate to make the inquiries, but given your submissions, you will have the normal time period in which to file your response.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: If I could just get a bit of an update. I know that there was a discussion at the 65 ter meeting yesterday on the subject of disclosure. I'd just like to confirm some points on the record to make sure that disclosure is proceeding appropriately. Obviously with respect to Mr. Stanisic there has been disclosure under 66(A)(i) completed quite a while ago. I understand that disclosure has now also been completed under 66(A)(i) in relation to Mr. Zupljanin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And, counsel, can you confirm that, just for me on the record? This is in relation to Rule 66(A)(i).

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Supporting materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Supporting materials have been provided. Okay. Now with regard to 66(A)(ii), I understand that the bulk of the disclosure has been completed, but there are some statements which are outstanding. Mr. Hannis, perhaps you could just confirm for me as to the state of that disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. What is outstanding are witness statements for a handsful of protected witnesses for whom we have delayed disclosure measures in place. And there is a possibly that we may be adding some witnesses in light of very recent investigation. But we haven't even filed a motion yet to amend our witness list, but if and when we do, we'll disclose that material promptly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Any comments on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Not for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm certain that I don't need to remind Mr. Hannis of his obligations under Rule 68. I'll just make mention that it's there and obviously there is the ongoing obligation at all times to disclose materials that fall within that rule.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the videolink microphone please be switched off. We can't hear the speakers in the courtroom, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I'm hoping that you've heard that in Belgrade so you can make that adjustment and keep the microphone off unless you need to turn it on to respond. Thank you. Now, the subject of agreed facts is something I did want to mention, again I know it was discussed yesterday at the status conference. The Trial Chamber is very interested and would like to encourage all the parties as much as possible to try and narrow down the issues in the case and try and come to agreement on those facts on which there is agreement, and therefore no necessity to add to the trial evidence relating to matters in which the parties can agree. And it's our view that that is of great importance to try and keep this proceeding very focused on the important issues. So I know that there have -- are renewed discussions with counsel for Mr. Stanisic, and I'm -- the Trial Chamber is very encouraged to hear that, and we would like you to make efforts from both sides to agree on facts not in dispute. I know that the position of the team for Mr. Zupljanin and the fact that you are in a -- that the file is newer than it is in the case of Mr. Stanisic, but I do want to emphasize that while of course time will be allowed for trial preparation, the Trial Chamber does want there to be a sense of movement and a sense of urgency to preparing and I'm certain counsel is aware of that. And it might benefit you at this stage just simply to have some participation in the discussions that are going on, because it will allow you to have a sense, at least, of what some of the agreed facts in issue or at play are. And so I would again, since all the parties are present when you have those opportunities, if you can take the opportunity to discuss potential agreed facts, appreciating, I appreciate what was conveyed, and it was conveyed to me by my senior legal officer, as to the state of preparations and the difficulties that you face at this stage, but I'm simply asking if you can at least engage in some preliminary discussions with both counsel for Mr. Stanisic and the Prosecution, I think that would be useful. Any comments on that, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if invited we shall certainly take part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I think -- Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They will be invited, Your Honour, and as I indicated yesterday. I had a very positive experience with both Mr. Visnjic and Mr. Zecevic in our past two years in the Milutinovic case. I'm optimistic that we will be able to reach agreement on a number of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thanks to all of you and I'm sure that will be the case as well. And I believe that was -- those were the only matters that I felt it necessary from this position of the Trial Chamber to raise today, however, aside from of course I will address the accused in relation to conditions. But before that, are there any issues -- perhaps I'll turn first to the Prosecution. Are there any issues that the Prosecution wishes to raise today, bring to the Trial Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Not that I can think of at the moment, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And Mr. Cvijetic in Belgrade, are there any matters that you wanted to bring to my attention this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing to raise by our Defence for the time being, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. While I have you, I'll do that in that order. Mr. Stanisic, any health matters that you wish to bring to my attention this afternoon? Anything you wanted to convey? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Nothing to report for the time being, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. I'm glad to hear that. Mr. Zupljanin, do you have any matters you wanted to bring to my attention in terms of either health issues, and if you do, and you wish to discuss them in private session, we can certainly do that, or any matters you want to bring to my attention regarding the conditions of your detention? THE ACCUSED ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Mrs. Prost, I have two questions, rather two issues. Firstly, tomorrow is a great day for my family and for me, St. Archangel Michael, which is our family feast day. I would like to take this opportunity to wish a very good holiday to all those celebrating and much joy while celebrating it. Secondly, I've been facing a lot of difficulty with my computer. This has been a difficult problem which has made it impossible for me to work on my defence to the extent I would have liked to. Before the start of this session, however, my lawyers have informed me that the computer issue will be dealt with over the following days. It will be to my great satisfaction if a solution arrives as soon as possible, Monday at the very latest, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I hope that that problem is resolved and I can understand that that is a significant problem in terms of trial preparation. So, Mr. Visnjic, if the problem continues and you feel the need to have the assistance of the Trial Chamber to the extent that is necessary, but I'm certain you can work that out with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. We were contacted by the Registrar this morning. I think at some point next week, the problem will be resolved. The problem being about the following: Mr. Zupljanin was unable to receive any materials served on him by the Prosecutor because of insufficient memory on his computer. And now he will hopefully be fully able to join in his own Defence and keep providing instructions to us in terms of what to do next. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Certainly. Thank you for bringing that to my attention. As I say, I'm sure that the problem will be fixed and you can proceed with trial preparations. Well, if there's nothing further then from any of the parties, this status conference is adjourned. Thank you and good afternoon to everyone.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
